question: Can people tell when a halo is shaping their own judgement?
answer: Rarely. Students watched one of two videos of a lecturer with a European accent, acting warm or cold. Those who saw him warm found his looks, mannerisms and accent appealing; those who saw him cold found them irritating. Both groups denied that liking him coloured those ratings; some insisted it ran the other way.
move: Ask whether the reasons came before the liking or after it.
